topic: Mastering the Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Perspective Shift
sections.content: Define 'Basis' as a coordinate system (a grid). Use an animation of a robot (Robby) standing in a 2D plane. Show that the same point in space can be described by different coordinate values depending on which grid (basis) Robby uses.
sections.example: Robby the Robot: Position (2, 3) in a standard grid vs. position (1, 1) in a tilted, stretched grid.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Basis and Linear Combinations
sections.content: Quickly recap that any vector v can be expressed as a unique linear combination of basis vectors: v = c1*b1 + c2*b2. Use a visual 'Vector Summation' animation where two arrows (basis vectors) are stacked head-to-tail to reach a target point.
sections.example: Representing vector v = [5, 7] as 5 times the unit vector 'i' plus 7 times the unit vector 'j'.

sections.title: The Change of Basis Matrix (P)
sections.content: Introduce the Transition Matrix P. Explain that P stores the old basis vectors expressed in terms of the new basis vectors as its columns. Provide the formula: [v]old = P * [v]new.
sections.example: A transformation matrix P that converts coordinates from a 'Standard Grid' to a 'Camera View' for a character in a game engine.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Computational Workflow
sections.content: Demonstrate the algorithm: 1. Identify the new basis vectors. 2. Construct the matrix P. 3. Multiply P by the coordinate vector to get the new representation. Visual aid: Use color-coded columns to show how basis vectors map into the matrix.
sections.example: Converting a coordinate from Basis B = { (1,0), (0,1) } to Basis B' = { (1,1), (-1,1) }.

sections.title: Real-World Synthesis & Wrap-up
sections.content: Conclude with an application: Why do we do this? It simplifies complex problems! Briefly show a physics simulation where changing the basis to align with an object's symmetry axis turns a difficult calculation into a simple diagonal matrix.
sections.example: A spinning propeller: Changing the basis to align with the blade's rotation axis to simplify the force vector calculations.
